entries.question: How are database migrations organised and applied?
entries.answer:
Migrations live in app/src/prisma/migrations, with one folder per migration, each named with a timestamp. The schema is defined in app/src/prisma/schema.prisma. The notes say the folder currently holds four migrations.

They are applied with `npx prisma migrate deploy`, and the database address comes from the DATABASE_URL environment variable.

The release checklist says to run `npx prisma migrate deploy` against a fresh database before a change ships. Each new migration also needs a one-line note explaining how to undo it.

# Migrations

Read from app/src/prisma/ and app/package.json.

The database schema is the Prisma file app/src/prisma/schema.prisma. Migrations live in app/src/prisma/migrations, one folder per migration, named with a timestamp. The folder has four migrations today. They are applied with npx prisma migrate deploy, and the database address comes from the DATABASE_URL environment variable.

# Release checklist

Before a change ships, run npx prisma migrate deploy against a fresh database. Every new migration needs a one line note saying how to undo it.

# JWT settings

Read from app/src/app/routes/auth/auth.ts and app/src/app/routes/auth/token.utils.ts.

Tokens are signed with HS256. The secret comes from the JWT_SECRET environment variable, and falls back to the string superSecret when it is not set. A token expires after 60 days.

Unit tests are Jest files named *.test.ts under app/src/tests/services and app/src/tests/utils. They are run with npx nx test api. The database is mocked in app/src/tests/prisma-mock.ts with jest-mock-extended, so these tests do not need Postgres. End to end tests are in the separate app/e2e folder.

A comment has a nullable timestamp field named editedAt. It stays null until the first edit. Each successful edit sets it to the time of the edit. The migration that adds it must not change existing rows.

# Test layout

Read from app/src/tests/ and app/jest.config.ts.

Unit tests are Jest files named *.test.ts under app/src/tests/services and app/src/tests/utils. They are run with npx nx test api. The database is mocked in app/src/tests/prisma-mock.ts with jest-mock-extended, so these tests do not need Postgres. End to end tests are in the separate app/e2e folder.

# Comment model fields

Read from app/src/prisma/schema.prisma.

The Comment model has the fields id, createdAt, updatedAt, body, articleId and authorId. It has no editedAt field and no deletedAt field today. Deleting a comment removes the row.

entries.question: How is an edited comment marked, and what must the migration that adds the mark do?
entries.answer:
An edited comment is marked by a nullable timestamp field named `editedAt`. It stays null until the first edit, and each successful edit sets it to the time of that edit.

The migration that adds the field must not change existing rows.

A comment belongs to the user in its authorId field. Deleting a comment looks it up by id and by the current user id together. entries.question: How must an API error response be shaped, and which status codes does it use?
entries.answer:
**Shape:** New error responses must be an object with an `errors` key that maps a field name to a list of messages, for example `{"errors":{"body":["can't be blank"]}}`. There is no extra wrapper object.

**Status codes:** The notes list three codes in use today:
- **422** for validation errors.
- **401** for a missing or bad token.
- **500** for any other error.

The notes don't say which status code a new error response should use. The 401 body in the current code (`{"status":"error","message":"missing authorization credentials"}`) doesn't follow the `errors` shape, so the notes don't say whether it counts as the body the app "already sends."

entries.answer: The notes don't say where the note must be written. The release checklist only requires that every new migration have a one-line note saying how to undo it, and it doesn't specify a file or location for that note.

entries.question: What happens to a comment when it is deleted, and which comments appear in comment lists?
entries.answer:
The notes conflict on what happens when a comment is deleted.

- **Soft-delete policy:** Deleting a comment sets a `deletedAt` timestamp and keeps the row. Comments with a `deletedAt` value are left out of comment lists.
- **Current schema:** The Comment model has no `deletedAt` field today, and deleting a comment removes the row.

The schema note reflects the current code, while the soft-delete note appears to describe the intended rule. The notes don't say which comments appear in lists under the current code. Only the comment author may delete a comment.

entries.question: Under the soft-delete policy, what is the name of the field that marks a comment as deleted, what type is it, and what value does a live comment hold?
entries.answer:
The notes do not contain a soft-delete policy, so I can't name a deletion field, its type, or a live-comment value.

The closest information is in the Comment model notes. They say the model has no `deletedAt` field today, and that deleting a comment removes the row. The notes also describe a nullable `editedAt` timestamp, but that marks edits, not deletions.
